units.title: A postcard for the previous owner

materials.title: A postcard for the previous owner
materials.text:

"Mrs Lin mentioned this friend when she gave us the keys. They exchanged pictures every spring."

Mum called Mrs Lin, who asked to ____2____ the card. On arriving, she held it silently. Her friend had moved abroad years earlier. Meetings were rare, but the postcards had ____3____. The friend apparently had not received her new address.

Through the window, I saw the apple tree. I had wanted it trimmed because its branches ____4____ the light. But Mrs Lin showed me an old photograph: she stood beneath it with the postcard's ____5____. They had planted it together.

"Would you like a new photograph?" I asked. She looked ____6____, then smiled.

Outside, I moved a chair so the trunk would be ____7____ in the picture. Mrs Lin stood beside it, holding the card. She sent the photograph with her correct ____8____ clearly below.

Next spring, a postcard arrived addressed to us. Her friend ____9____ us for the photograph. We replied with a picture of the first flowers.

We still trimmed the tree when necessary. Caring about its story did not mean leaving every branch ____10____. But it was no longer merely an ____11____ outside the window. It connected our home with lives that had been there ____12____ us.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Mum recognises the signed name as the friend Mrs Lin mentioned. Copying, improving and hiding do not describe identifying a familiar name.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Mrs Lin comes to collect the card already at the new house. Deliver would bring it there, print produce a copy and replace substitute another card.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Yearly cards maintained contact despite rare meetings: continued. Stopped and failed contradict the ongoing card; changed does not express the sustained exchange described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Branches reduce incoming light, so blocked. Measuring does not affect it, and reflected/produced would add or redirect light rather than create the stated obstruction.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The friend pictured with Mrs Lin is the sender whose continuing cards are explained. Buyer, artist and reader are unestablished roles.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: An unexpected offer followed by a smile suggests pleased surprise. Anger, boredom and shame have no support in this response.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: Moving an obstructing chair makes the trunk clear in the photograph. Invisible reverses the purpose; smaller and distant concern scale or position rather than removing the obstruction.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: The wrongly routed card arose from an old address, so she now gives the correct address. Age and price do not route mail, and a password is neither needed nor appropriate to the exchange.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: A new friendly postcard acknowledges the helpful photograph by thanking them. Blame, a charge and a warning conflict with the appreciative exchange.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: They still trim necessary branches, so do not leave all untouched. Unnoticed concerns attention rather than pruning; broken and painted are not the care choices described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: Blocking light made the tree seem an obstacle. Invitation, instrument and experiment do not describe the earlier inconvenience.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: Previous residents lived there before the new family. Beside describes location, without absence and against opposition, not the sequence of inhabitants.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: The misdirected card gives a reason to listen to the home's history. It creates no rule, debt or danger warning.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: The new exchange continues the tree's story. It is not bought, established as a disputed proof or hidden.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: An annual spring photograph becomes a tradition. Repeated intentional exchange is not an accident, contest or problem.

units.title: The morning we missed the sunrise

materials.title: The morning we missed the sunrise
materials.text:
I promised four friends a sunrise view from a hilltop at six. After checking the route and sharing our departure time, my plan seemed ____1____.

Daniel arrived ten minutes late with a flat bicycle tyre. I wanted to ____2____ him for spoiling the schedule. Then he apologised: he had walked the last two kilometres.

We climbed quickly. As the sky grew pale, I checked my watch repeatedly. My friends tried to talk, but I answered ____3____, saving breath for the hill.

Daniel stopped beside a wall. I assumed he needed another ____4____. Instead, he pointed to mist between the fields and light touching the trees.

"Look!"

"We must reach the top," I replied. Nobody moved. One friend took photographs; another sat on the wall. They were ____5____ the morning I was hurrying past.

I turned. It was not the view I had ____6____, but it was beautiful. I pocketed my watch and joined them.

At the summit, the sun was already above the horizon. The promised moment was ____7____. Nevertheless, we stayed, sharing breakfast and finding our route in the valley below.

Daniel later offered to pay for drinks because he had delayed us. I ____8____. He had made a real effort to come.

That evening, our group chat filled with photographs. Few showed the summit; most showed mist, breakfast and friends. I had nearly judged everything against one ____9____.

I still plan departure times: keeping promises ____10____. But plans should ____11____ an experience, not make me blind to it. Next time, I will allow more room for the ____12____. When timing changes, I hope to notice what remains ____13____. We missed the advertised sunrise, but not the chance to spend a morning ____14____. Those things, I learned, were not ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Checked route and communicated timing make the plan appear complete. No cost or secrecy is discussed, and the organiser believes it possible.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The organiser initially wants to blame Daniel for the delay. Reward and introduce do not express annoyance, and follow does not respond to the spoiled schedule.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Saving breath means short, brief answers. Politeness and honesty are not the length distinction; loudly would use rather than save breath.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: The organiser assumes a stop means another rest during the climb. A map, bicycle or promise is not the expected recovery pause.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Taking photographs and sitting to appreciate the view shows enjoying it. Predicting concerns the future, repairing an object and advertising public promotion, not appreciating the present scene.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: The valley view differs from the planned summit sunrise. It is not a forgotten view, a measured quantity or a borrowed possession.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The sun is already up when they arrive, so the sunrise moment was missed. Recorded and repeated imply capturing or experiencing it; created does not fit a natural event they cannot produce.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: The organiser refuses the payment offer after recognising Daniel's effort. Agreed would accept it, waited merely postpones a response, and vanished would mean leaving rather than responding.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Reaching the summit at sunrise was one target. Friend, camera and valley do not name the fixed standard used to judge the outing.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The organiser still respects departure times because promises matter. Changes and disappears do not explain that value, while waits is not an appropriate claim about keeping a promise.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: A plan should support the experience, not displace attention to it. Replace and prevent undermine the experience; hide conceals it rather than enables it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: The unplanned valley view illustrates leaving room for the unexpected. Price, speed and proximity are not the category of discovery.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Even changed timing leaves worthwhile things possible. Silence, identicality and formality do not express remaining opportunities.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: Five friends still spend the morning together. They are outdoors and not alone, with no foreign travel described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Missing a scheduled sunrise and missing shared time are not identical. The passage distinguishes them, not their usefulness, simplicity or necessity.
